title: Chicken leg, drumstick and thigh, stewed, skin eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Stewed chicken parts – leg, drumstick and thigh – are pieces of meat with skin cooked by slow simmering in liquid. This method makes the meat tender while the skin becomes flavorful and slightly crisp. The product is commonly used in stews, soups, or served as a main dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken legs and thighs contain more connective tissue than breast meat, making them ideal for long cooking.
Stewed skin retains some of its fat, giving the dish a rich taste.
In many traditional cuisines (e.g., Russian, Polish, American) stewed chicken parts are considered classic comfort food.
When cooked properly the meat stays juicy and the skin can become lightly crisp if finished with a quick sear.
Stewed chicken pieces are often added to broths to deepen flavor.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken meat provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Stewed parts are a source of vitamin B6 and niacin, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: The product supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood formation, immunity and bone health.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and skin fat helps keep you feeling full for longer.

items.title: Contains collagen
items.content: Skin‑on chicken retains collagen, which may benefit skin elasticity and joint health.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Chicken parts with skin are richer in fat, so portion control is advisable for those watching calorie intake.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improper cooking can leave pathogens (e.g., Salmonella) alive. Ensure internal temperature reaches at least 74 °C (165 °F).

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium in prepared dishes
items.content: Stewed products made with added salt or sauces can be high in sodium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Stewed legs, drumsticks and thighs can be served as a standalone portion, added to soups, stews, salads, or used in sandwiches. The skin can be eaten together with the meat or briefly pan‑fried for extra crispness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked product in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in sealed bags at –18 °C (0 °F) where it retains quality for 2‑3 months. Reheat thoroughly before consumption.
